strings.d1.s0.name: Brandenburger Tor
strings.d1.s0.tips: Pariser Platz is empty in the morning; look through the gate towards the Tiergarten.
strings.d1.s1.name: Holocaust Memorial
strings.d1.s1.tips: 2,711 concrete blocks; the underground information centre is free.
strings.d1.s2.name: Reichstag Dome
strings.d1.s2.tips: Free, but book online 2-3 weeks ahead (bring ID). Glass dome with audio guide and city views.
strings.d1.s3.name: Mustafa's Gemüse Kebap
strings.d1.s3.tips: The legendary vegetable doner on Mehringdamm. Expect a 30-60 minute queue, shorter at lunchtime.
strings.d1.s4.name: Gendarmenmarkt
strings.d1.s4.tips: Berlin's most beautiful square, with its twin cathedrals and the Konzerthaus.
strings.d1.b0.name: Curry 36 Mehringdamm
strings.d1.b0.tips: Currywurst opposite Mustafa's, if there's no queue.
strings.d1.b1.name: Berlin Cathedral
strings.d1.b1.tips: Climb the cathedral dome (270 steps); right by Museum Island.
strings.d2.s0.name: Pergamonmuseum Das Panorama
strings.d2.s0.tips: The main building is closed until 2027; the Ishtar Gate panorama and Pergamon pieces are in the neighbouring building.
strings.d2.s1.name: Neues Museum
strings.d2.s1.tips: Home of the Nefertiti bust. Book a timed ticket online; the Museum Island day pass is 24 EUR.
strings.d2.s2.name: Alte Nationalgalerie
strings.d2.s2.tips: Caspar David Friedrich and the German Romantics.
strings.d2.s3.name: Hackescher Markt Yemek
strings.d2.s3.tips: The courtyards of the Hackesche Höfe, with cafes and street food.
strings.d2.s4.name: Hackesche Höfe & Haus Schwarzenberg
strings.d2.s4.tips: Art nouveau courtyards and the graffiti-covered Schwarzenberg courtyard (Anne Frank Zentrum).
strings.d2.b0.name: Bode Museum
strings.d2.b0.tips: Byzantine art and sculpture, at the tip of the island by the river.
strings.d2.b1.name: Zeit für Brot Alte Schönhauser
strings.d2.b1.tips: Bakery known for its cinnamon rolls.
strings.d3.theme: The Wall: Bernauer and East Side
strings.d3.s0.name: Berlin Wall Memorial Bernauer Strasse
strings.d3.s0.tips: An original section of the Wall, the death strip and a documentation centre. The most honest account of the Wall, and free.
strings.d3.s1.name: Mauerpark
strings.d3.s1.tips: Flea market and karaoke on Sundays; on other days, a park with Wall graffiti.
strings.d3.s2.name: Prenzlauer Berg Kollwitzplatz
strings.d3.s2.tips: Cafes and Kastanienallee; market Thursday to Saturday.
strings.d3.s3.name: Konnopke's Imbiss
strings.d3.s3.tips: Currywurst under the U-Bahn tracks since 1930, an East Berlin classic.
strings.d3.s4.name: East Side Gallery
strings.d3.s4.tips: 1.3 km of paintings on the Wall, including the Brezhnev-Honecker kiss. Walk on to Oberbaumbrücke.
strings.d3.b0.name: Burgermeister Schlesisches Tor
strings.d3.b0.tips: Burgers in a former public toilet building, near the East Side Gallery.
strings.d3.b1.name: Checkpoint Charlie
strings.d3.b1.tips: A tourist crossing point; the Mauermuseum charges admission. Choose it instead of East Side.
strings.d4.s0.name: Markthalle Neun
strings.d4.s0.tips: Kreuzberg's market hall: Street Food Thursday, and a market on Saturday.
strings.d4.s1.name: Landwehrkanal Walk
strings.d4.s1.tips: A stroll along the canal; the Turkish market at Maybachufer runs Tuesday to Friday.
strings.d4.s2.name: Tempelhofer Feld
strings.d4.s2.tips: A vast, windswept open space in winter; keep the walk short.
strings.d4.s3.name: Neukölln Weserstrasse
strings.d4.s3.tips: Bars and cafes in Berlin's young neighbourhood.
strings.d4.s4.name: Hamy Cafe Neukölln
strings.d4.s4.tips: Vietnamese cuisine; a cheap Neukölln favourite.
strings.d4.b0.name: Rüyam Gemüse Kebab
strings.d4.b1.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
strings.d4.b1.tips: A Libeskind building; choose it over Tempelhof in the rain.
strings.d5.s0.name: Charlottenburg Palace
strings.d5.s0.tips: Prussian palace with a baroque garden: the Altes Schloss and Neuer Flügel.
strings.d5.s1.name: Charlottenburg Palace Gardens
strings.d5.s1.tips: The palace gardens, with a lake; free.
strings.d5.s2.name: Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
strings.d5.s2.tips: A bombed-out tower beside the new church with its blue glass.
strings.d5.s3.name: KaDeWe 6th Floor Food Hall
strings.d5.s3.tips: Europe's largest food hall; eat oysters or wurst at the counter.
strings.d5.s4.name: Bikini Berlin & Zoo
strings.d5.s4.tips: A concept mall with a terrace overlooking the zoo (Monkey Bar).
strings.d5.b0.name: Schwarzes Café
strings.d5.b1.name: Berlin Zoo
strings.d5.b1.tips: Germany's oldest zoo; choose it instead of the mall.
strings.d6.s0.name: Sanssouci Palace
strings.d6.s0.tips: 40 minutes on the S7. Frederick's palace with vineyard terraces; timed ticket.
strings.d6.s1.name: Sanssouci Park
strings.d6.s1.tips: Walk through the park to the Chinese House and the New Palace; 300 hectares.
strings.d6.s2.name: Dutch Quarter Potsdam
strings.d6.s2.tips: The Dutch Quarter, with red-brick houses and cafes.
strings.d6.s3.name: Maison Charlotte Potsdam
strings.d6.s3.tips: A French bistro in the Dutch Quarter.
strings.d6.s4.name: Cecilienhof
strings.d6.s4.tips: The country house where the 1945 Potsdam Conference took place; see the Truman-Stalin-Churchill table.
strings.d6.b0.name: Potsdam Brauhaus
strings.d6.b1.name: Glienicke Bridge
strings.d6.b1.tips: The spy bridge; choose it instead of Cecilienhof.
strings.d7.s0.name: Berlin TV Tower
strings.d7.s0.tips: The 203 m TV tower. Book the first slot of the morning online; it has a revolving restaurant.
strings.d7.s1.name: Nikolaiviertel
strings.d7.s1.tips: Berlin's oldest quarter (rebuilt), with the Nikolaikirche.
strings.d7.s2.name: Zur Letzten Instanz
strings.d7.s2.tips: Berlin's oldest restaurant, open since 1621; try the eisbein (boiled pork knuckle).
strings.d7.s3.name: Alexanderplatz World Clock
strings.d7.s3.tips: The World Time Clock. The Airport Express to BER takes 30 minutes: time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Curry 61 Alexanderplatz
strings.d7.b1.name: DDR Museum
strings.d7.b1.tips: An interactive museum of everyday life in East Germany.
strings.note0: A BVG day ticket for zones AB costs about 9 EUR; the Berlin WelcomeCard covers transport plus discounts. The FEX/S9 to BER takes 30-40 minutes. Cycling is ideal in this flat city.
strings.note1: The Reichstag dome is free, but you must register online 2-3 weeks ahead. Museum Island uses timed tickets, and entry is free on the first Sunday of the month (Museumssonntag).
strings.note2: Winter is 0-5°C and grey, and it gets dark by 16:00. Museums are a good bet, and in December there are Christmas markets (Gendarmenmarkt); January is cheap.
strings.note3: Doner is 6-8 EUR (Mustafa's, Rüyam), currywurst 4-5 EUR, and a restaurant meal 15-25 EUR. Tip 5-10% by rounding up; cash is still common.
strings.note4: Shops are closed on Sundays. The Mauerpark flea market is on Sundays, and Markthalle Neun is busiest on Thursday evening.
strings.note5: Clubs (Berghain) run Friday to Sunday; the door policy is selective, so wear black. Photos are banned.
